value_unit: retry only with idempotency or successful reconciliation
decision_rationale: The first pass correctly rejected blind registration POST retry. The second-order pass preserves that negative invariant and generalizes it into a target-wide authority: replay is permitted only for intrinsic idempotency or owner-supplied read-only reconciliation; unreconcilable creates remain single-attempt.
invariant: ambiguous remote writes are never replayed without an explicit proof of replay safety
negative_invariant: never turn a generic POST retry loop into authority for non-idempotent side effects
migration_impact: additive policy owner and call-site classification

value_unit: bounded Retry-After-aware mutation pacing separated from provider error parsing
decision_rationale: Aether separated structured provider errors and Retry-After hints from retry policy. LumiNet now centralizes bounded Retry-After/backoff/cancellation mechanics while provider owners continue to interpret their own responses and reconciliation state.
invariant: retry timing is bounded and caller cancellation wins
negative_invariant: provider error text or Retry-After alone never makes a mutation replay-safe
migration_impact: additive shared policy and provider integration

value_unit: source freshness and due-refresh pacing inside the canonical profile owner
decision_rationale: The donor TTL cache remains the conceptual source, but a separate cache would duplicate profile authority. Its useful freshness idea is recomposed into ProfileService scheduling using LastUpdated, interval, in-flight ownership, and bounded source backoff.
target_capability: subscription source health and automatic refresh
invariant: only active opted-in profiles are automatically refreshed when due and outside source backoff
negative_invariant: do not create a second subscription catalog/cache authority
migration_impact: additive profile evidence and service-owned scheduler

decision_rationale: The donor value is concise source-specific failure explanation. LumiNet keeps that outcome but routes it through the existing redaction owner, caps persisted/operator-visible text, and records backoff state rather than storing raw fetch errors.
invariant: source failures are bounded, redacted, URL-stale-safe evidence
negative_invariant: never persist subscription credentials or raw secret-bearing fetch errors in source health

value_unit: desktop update workflow second-order promotion decision
decision_rationale: A larger updater plane is valuable only if artifact identity, signature verification, atomic promotion, rollback, and crash recovery share one target authority. The current repository still has no such signed promotion authority, so making donor download/update UX live would reduce safety.
negative_invariant: never auto-promote downloaded executable content without authenticated artifact identity and rollback authority

value_unit: release discovery/update tooling second-order promotion decision
decision_rationale: Release discovery by itself is not a safe updater. Without a signed manifest and rollback owner it would create an attractive but unauthoritative download path, so the mechanism remains reference-only.
negative_invariant: release metadata must never become executable update authority by URL freshness alone

value_unit: cross-donor release asset/TTL update plane second-order promotion decision
decision_rationale: The cross-donor convergence makes the product value clear, but none of the donors supplies the missing target trust root, atomic promotion contract, or rollback authority. The larger plane therefore remains deliberately non-live rather than being assembled from unsigned pieces.
negative_invariant: do not compose multiple unsigned updater fragments into a de facto update authority

decision_rationale: The first pass already hardened ProcessSupervisor correctly, but it still has no production constructor. Wiring it now around existing Tor/runtime owners would create a second lifecycle authority, so the capability remains dormant rather than being falsely presented as shipped recovery.
negative_invariant: do not create a second process restart/cancellation owner around an already-owned runtime

decision_rationale: The readiness primitive remains useful and already hardened in the dormant target supervisor, but no production seam justifies transferring runtime authority to it.
negative_invariant: readiness detection must not imply lifecycle ownership where none was promoted

decision_rationale: The operator workflow remains useful design reference, but promoting it as a new host-mutation plane would bypass LumiNet authenticated system/diagnostic ownership. No second host authority is introduced.
negative_invariant: host mutations remain behind existing authenticated system ownership and must not be duplicated in a donor-shaped GUI plane

decision_rationale: The hardened LumiCore DiagnosticRunbook remains a sound public capability, but it still has no production caller while the daemon already owns diagnostic jobs, APIs, lifecycle, persistence, and operator export. Promoting the dormant Rust runbook into runtime orchestration would create a parallel diagnostics authority rather than add a missing capability.
negative_invariant: do not create a second diagnostic orchestration/lifecycle authority beside the daemon diagnostics job and API plane

value_unit: SSTP transport/profile plane second-order promotion decision
separability: context-dependent on transport authority and platform support
decision_rationale: A second-order review still does not justify promotion: SSTP would add a parallel transport, credential, TLS, and platform lifecycle authority without target-native protocol ownership or platform verification. The donor remains useful protocol reference, but importing it would weaken the single-owner transport model and could carry weaker TLS assumptions.
negative_invariant: do not add an unverified parallel VPN transport/credential plane or inherit weaker TLS defaults
